name: a-post-that-truly-failed-is-still-a-gap
rule: A comments edge that fails for any reason OTHER than Meta's (#100) is still a gap: the answer is partial and says the post could not be read. Only (#100) means 'no comments'.
why: T-55, and it exists because the first version of that case did not catch its own opposite. `an-absent-comments-edge-is-no-comments` passed with the predicate mutated to `error instanceof MetaApiError` — every failure reclassified as 'this post has no comments'. That mutation turns an expired token, a permission refusal or an upstream 500 into a confident zero, which is the exact failure the whole capability exists to prevent and the one an-ad-with-no-page-post-says-so guards from the other side. A widening fix needs a case that objects to the widening.

data.message: the post whose comments read normally
the post this token may not read
